The fact says hypothyroidism, which contradicts the doctor's recorded interpretation, though it matches the patient's original statement.

Doctor concludes, 'It looks like... it is quite widespread, your eczema,' with very itchy, sore, red, dry rash on flexural areas ('inside of the elbows... Which is the, the worst area'), consistent with an extensive atopic dermatitis flare.
Patient is 'still using the steroids' (OTC hydrocortisone) but it is 'not helping,' and previously 'tried' OTC antihistamines which 'didn't work,' indicating refractoriness.

Doctor asks, 'Otherwise, other than those rash, you're feeling well in yourself. There's no temperature, no joint pains, yeah? No fever?' and no systemic complaints are reported, indicating patient is systemically well and afebrile.
Asthma described as using 'The blue inhaler... on and off' and patient says, 'It's only when I have a flare,' implying intermittent and currently stable asthma.
Doctor says, 'you would probably need some antihistamines, which I'm going to prescribe... it's called the antihistamine is called Fexofenadine,' without specifying exact dose/frequency.
Doctor plans, 'we'll try with some Betnovate first... You, you have to use it twice a day, for the next couple of weeks.' This matches a thin layer topical steroid twice daily for about 2 weeks.
Doctor instructs, 'You still need to continue on your, emollients like the dermal soap, and, as well as the, diprovate. Yeah, so you still need to use those.'

Doctor advises, 'If, if there's no improvement, you need to get back to us. Or, if you have any kind of adverse reaction... you need to get in touch with us... If things are getting worse in the next two weeks, call us before hand. Otherwise, wait for two weeks.'
Doctor confirms, 'we're going to send off the prescription to your pharmacy... it looks like Boots on the systems, is that correct?... so i'll send it across to Boot's.'
